headline: Record revenue, margins, and cash flow to close the year
summary_short: NetApp's fiscal fourth-quarter revenue rose 12% y/y to $1,948M with record gross profit and operating income, as basic EPS climbed to $2.05 from $1.67 a year earlier.
summary_long: NetApp's fiscal fourth-quarter revenue rose 12% y/y to $1,948M, led by record all-flash array revenue (+18% y/y to $1.2B) and record Public Cloud revenue (+11% y/y to $182M). Gross profit rose 14% y/y to $1,365M and operating income rose to $531M as total operating expenses were roughly flat y/y. Net income was $404M ($2.05 basic EPS, $2.03 diluted), both up double digits y/y. Free cash flow was $900M, up 41% y/y; NetApp returned $1.36B to shareholders via buybacks and dividends in FY2026. For Q1 FY2027 the company guided GAAP revenue to $1.75-$1.90B and GAAP EPS to $1.35-$1.45. Cash and investments stood at $3,584M.

drivers.explanation: Growth was driven by record all-flash array revenue (+18% y/y to $1.2B) and record Public Cloud revenue (+11% y/y to $182M), per the release's own segment highlights.
Not explained in the release beyond the record all-flash and Public Cloud revenue growth already cited for the top line.

Operating income grew faster than revenue because total operating expenses were roughly flat y/y ($833M vs $845M a year ago) while revenue rose 12%, per our own decomposition of the release's income statement.

Net income grew despite the effective tax rate rising to 22.0% from 4.0% a year ago (which had benefited from a resolution of income tax matters); operating income growth outweighed the higher tax expense.
EPS growth tracks net income growth and also benefited from a lower diluted share count (199M vs 206M a year ago) following FY2026 buybacks.
NetApp issued initial Q1 FY2027 and full-FY2027 guidance alongside record FY2026 results across revenue, gross profit, operating income, and free cash flow, per CEO George Kurian's release quote.
